48:Names as they appear in the prototype. The prototype's own state catalog has 32 entries: Tela 0 — Splash; Tela 0.1 — Biometria; Tela 0.1a — Entrar / criar conta; Tela 0.1b — PIN inicial; Tela 0.1c — PIN após falha; Tela 1 — Home / Chat; Tela 2 — Texto, Áudio (Gravando, Processando, Transcrito, Erro), Foto (Captura, Processando OCR, Reconhecido, Erro); Tela 3 — Menu lateral; Tela 1 — Sessão expirada; Tela 4 — Meus Registros, Estado vazio, Sheet de filtro, Filtros ativos; Exportar — Pendente, Processando, Concluído, Erro, Período vazio; Tela 5 — Planos de Ação **[ext]**; Tela 6 — Configurações, Dashboard zero entradas, Dashboard uma entrada, Narrativa indisponível, Confirmar exclusão. The tables below group them by screen; some rows describe variations inside one state (e.g., the bookmark sub-states, the streaming response). Extension states (requirements, section 2) are marked **[ext]**.
49-
50-### 2.1 Entry and authentication
51-| State | What it shows |
52-|---|---|
53-| Tela 0 — Splash | Wordmark "Cerne" centered on dark green, 3 loading dots; lasts 1.8 s and moves on automatically. |
54:| Tela 0.1 — Biometria | Fingerprint circle, title "Toque para desbloquear", link "Usar PIN", secondary link "usar e-mail e senha" near the bottom. |
55:| Tela 0.1a — Entrar | Login mode: title "Bem-vindo de volta", fields E-mail and Senha, CTA "Entrar", toggle link, link "usar biometria". |
56:| Tela 0.1a — Criar conta | Same screen in sign-up mode: title "Crie sua conta", CTA "Criar conta" (toggled by a text link, not a separate screen). |
57:| Tela 0.1b — PIN inicial | Title "Digite seu PIN", 4 progress dots, 3×4 numeric keypad with backspace; after the 4th digit, moves on after 350 ms. |
58:| Tela 0.1c — PIN após falha | Same as 0.1b plus the error band "Não foi possível reconhecer — digite seu PIN". |
59-
60-### 2.2 Conversation
61-| State | What it shows |
62-|---|---|
63-| Tela 1 — Home/Chat (default) | Messages going back and forth; dark green fixed header with ☰ and wordmark; composer with "+", placeholder "Escreva uma mensagem...", send icon. |
64-| Tela 1 — Streaming | AI response revealed progressively with a pulsing cursor. |
65-| Tela 1 — Insight | Insight card with ochre spine, label "INSIGHT", "x" to dismiss, interleaved in the messages. |
66-| Tela 1 — Falha ao gerar resposta | Incomplete AI message with "Falha ao gerar resposta — toque para tentar novamente" in red, in place of the time. |
67-| Tela 1 — Bookmark | Bookmark on each user message with 4 sub-states: `idle`, `saving` (spinner), `saved` (ochre check), `error` (red warning). |
68-| Tela 1 — Offline | Blue-gray banner "Sem conexão — histórico disponível, novas mensagens bloqueadas"; send icon disabled. |
69-| Tela 1 — Sessão expirada | Light scrim over the chat (still readable), centered card with lock icon, title "Sessão expirada", text saying history and scroll position are kept, button "Entrar novamente". |
70-| Tela 3 — Menu lateral | Drawer: initials avatar and name; section "CONVERSAS" with past sessions (title + timestamp); items "Meus Registros", "Planos de Ação", "Configurações"; new-conversation action. |
71-
72-### 2.3 Insertion modal (bottom sheet over Home/Chat; 9 states)
73-Common structure: "x" to close and a 3-tab bar (Texto / Áudio / Foto); the active tab has a filled dark-green background.
74-
75-| State | What it shows |
76-|---|---|
77-| Texto | Multiline field, placeholder "Escreva livremente...", button "Salvar". |
78-| Áudio — Gravando | Red stop button, animated 12-bar waveform, monospace timer (e.g., "00:12"). |
79-| Áudio — Processando | Spinner in place of stop; frozen, faded waveform (opacity .35); text "Transcrevendo..."; label "00:42 de áudio". |
80-| Áudio — Transcrito | Editable transcribed text; original audio duration in mono; "Salvar" enabled. |
81-| Áudio — Erro | Red warning icon, "Não foi possível transcrever", outline button "Tentar novamente". |
82-| Foto — Captura | Two large buttons, "Câmera" and "Galeria". |
83-| Foto — Processando OCR | Photo thumbnail, spinner, "Reconhecendo texto...". |
84-| Foto — Reconhecido | Small thumbnail next to the extracted (editable) text; "Salvar". |
85-| Foto — Erro | Thumbnail kept, warning icon, "Não foi possível reconhecer o texto", button "Tentar novamente" and secondary text action "Salvar só a foto". |
86-
87-### 2.4 Records
88-| State | What it shows |
89-|---|---|
90-| Tela 4 — Meus Registros (default) | Records grouped by date ("Hoje", "Ontem", dates); each card with a spine colored by origin, source icon, time, sync indicator (green "sincronizado" / ochre "sincronizando" / red "erro de sync"), text excerpt, category chips when present; header with back arrow, title, download icon; search bar "Buscar nos registros..." with a funnel button. |
91-| Tela 4 — Vazio | Large notebook icon, "Nenhum registro ainda", CTA "Criar primeiro registro". |
92-| Tela 4 — Filtros ativos | Removable chips under the search bar with the applied filters, link "Limpar filtros"; funnel button filled. |
93-| Tela 4 — Sheet de filtro | Groups "INTERVALO DE DATA" (Todo o período / Esta semana / Este mês, single choice), "CATEGORIA" (chips: trabalho, rotina, descanso, relações), "TIPO DE ENTRADA" (chips: manual, áudio, foto, chat); "Aplicar" and "Limpar". **Note:** the backend has no category filter (requirements, RF06); categories are the tags extension. |
94-
95-### 2.5 Export (bottom sheet over Tela 4; 5 states)
96-| State | What it shows |
97-|---|---|
98-| Pendente | Spinner, "Preparando exportação...". |
99-| Processando | "Gerando resumo com IA...", progress bar. |
100-| Concluído | Green check, "Resumo pronto", buttons "Baixar PDF" (primary) and "Baixar dados brutos" (outline). |
101-| Erro | Red warning; text explaining that the AI narrative failed but the data remains available; only the button "Baixar dados brutos". |
102-| Período vazio | "Nenhum registro nesse período." and a suggestion to adjust the filter; no download button. |
103-
104-All five have the link "Fechar" at the bottom. The mapping between these states and the backend job statuses is in `docs/input/backend/export-screen-states.md`.
105-
106-### 2.6 Plans and settings
107-| State | What it shows |
108-|---|---|
109-| Tela 5 — Planos de Ação **[ext]** | Three horizontally scrolling columns — "A Fazer", "Em Andamento", "Concluído" — with counts and cards. |
110-| Tela 6 — Configurações — mais de 30 registros | "Sua evolução": 10-bar ochre chart + summary paragraph. |
111-| Tela 6 — Configurações — uma entrada | A single small bar and the text "Ainda é cedo pra ver um padrão — volte em alguns dias." |
112-| Tela 6 — Configurações — zero entradas | Light-gray chart icon in place of the chart and "Comece a registrar para ver sua evolução aqui"; no summary paragraph. |
113-| Tela 6 — Configurações — narrativa indisponível | Chart with data, but the AI summary paragraph failed — needs its own error message, not just missing text. |
114-| Tela 6 — Confirmar exclusão de conta | Centered dialog, red title "Apagar sua conta?", text on permanent, irreversible deletion; red button "Apagar tudo"; outline "Cancelar". |
115-
116-Other elements of Configurações: avatar with editable name/e-mail (pencil becomes a check in edit mode — inline editing); persona cards "Como a IA responde" (Analítico, Empático, Socrático) **[ext]**; actions "Sair" and "Apagar conta" (red).
117-
118----
--
228:| PIN keypad | Tela 0.1b/c | digits 0–9 + backspace; progress dots above |
229-| Tab bar | Insertion modal | 3 tabs (Texto/Áudio/Foto), active tab with filled background |
230-| Audio waveform | Insertion modal, Áudio tab | active/animated (recording) · frozen and faded (processing) |
231-| Skeleton | Any content loaded over the network | shown for calls longer than 300 ms (RNF01) |

## 4. Other non-functional requirements

RNF01 — Interaction latency (a local action is reflected in the UI in < 100 ms; any network call above 300 ms shows a loading indicator) · RNF02 — PII stripping (via Claude Haiku 4.5 with a structured prompt / tool use, not a dedicated NER model) · RNF03 — Zero data retention · RNF04 — RLS (Row Level Security) · RNF05 — Hard delete of account and data (LGPD).

**Known limitation:** the system has no protocol for detecting or responding to risk signals (suicidal ideation, self-harm) in entries or chat messages. Since the product is not framed as a mental-health app, this absence is an explicit scope decision.

---

## 5. Interface architecture and screen flow

### 5.1 Visual foundation (design system)
Minimalist identity, a warm and neutral palette, readable sans-serif typography, standardized components (buttons, chat bubbles, cards). This foundation is the direct object of RNF08. Tokens: `docs/input/prototype/prototype-extract.md`.

### 5.2 Screens

**Screen 0 — Splash:** initial loading; checks the connection and syncs the cache in the background. *Connects to: RF06, RNF01.*

**Screen 0.1 — Authentication vault:** biometric/PIN barrier before access. *Connects to: RF03.*

**Screen 1 — Home (chat):** main screen, continuous conversation, "+" button for multimodal input, AI status indicator, "save to journal" button on each user message. *Connects to: RF04, RF08, RF10, RNF01, RNF09.*

**Screen 2 — Insertion Modal:** overlay with three ways to capture — raw text field, microphone (audio) and gallery/camera (photo) — with a transcription indicator. Every capture here creates a persisted entry, never a chat message. *Connects to: RF01, RF02.*

**Screen 3 — Side menu (sidebar):** navigation hub, session history, access to My Records / Action Plans / Settings, and a "Novo Chat" button that opens Screen 1 in its empty state. *Connects to: RF04 (via the "Novo Chat" button); the other items are pure navigation.*

**Screen 4 — My Records:** consolidated timeline, filters, manual tags (extension, section 2), export. *Connects to: RF07, RF06, RF05.*

**Screen 5 — Action Plans:** simple Kanban board (columns "A Fazer" / "Em Andamento" / "Concluído") with static example cards. *(Extension — section 2.)*

**Screen 6 — Settings and profile:** evolution dashboard, persona selector — "Analítico" / "Empático" / "Socrático" (extension, section 2; it would only change the system-prompt string of RF04), delete account. *Connects to: RF09, RNF05.*

---

## 6. Backend endpoint inventory

The backend is already built and frozen. The API contract, `docs/input/backend/api/openapi.yaml`, is the source of truth; this section is a reading of it oriented by screen and requirement. How to build the real URL of each operation: `docs/input/backend/README.md`.

Every endpoint returns errors in the standard contract of RNF09 — `{ code, message, retryable }` — and is protected by RLS in Supabase. AI providers: Claude (chat, vision/OCR, summary, insights, dashboard, PII detection) and Voyage AI (embeddings) — the backend's only two external AI dependencies. Audio transcription (speech-to-text) runs on-device (Whisper) and never reaches the backend as an audio file.

### 6.1 Authentication and session
| Endpoint | Requirement | AI involved |
|---|---|---|
| `POST /auth/signup` | RF03 | — |
| `POST /auth/login` | RF03 | — |
| `POST /auth/refresh` | RF03, RF07 | — |
| `GET /auth/session` | RF07 | — |
| `POST /auth/logout` | RF03 | — |

**No "biometric-unlock" endpoint — intentional:** the Face ID / Touch ID / PIN barrier of Screen 0.1 is validated entirely on the device, never on the server. The backend only stores the preference (`biometricEnabled`, read and written via `PATCH /account/settings`, section 6.7) — it validates no biometrics. After passing the local barrier, the app uses the existing session (renewed via `POST /auth/refresh` when needed, or `POST /auth/login` if it has fully expired).

### 6.2 Ingestion and entries
| Endpoint | Requirement | AI involved |
|---|---|---|
| `POST /media/ocr` — the image is not persisted; only the extracted text moves on | RF02 | Claude Haiku 4.5 (vision) |
| `POST /entries` — creates an entry; internally triggers the PII check and embedding generation; accepts `source` (`manual`/`audio`/`photo`/`chat`) and `chatMessageId` when the origin is the chat | RF01, RF02, RF10 | Claude Haiku 4.5 (PII) + Voyage AI (embedding) |
| `GET /entries` — filters by `source`/`dateFrom`/`dateTo`; tags appear only embedded in the response, read-only | RF07 | — |
| `GET /entries/:id` | RF07 | — |

**No entry editing or deletion, and no tag endpoint — intentional:** entries are immutable once created ("original content intact, never censored"); there is no `PATCH`/`DELETE /entries/:id`. Tags are populated only by test seed data — no endpoint creates, deletes or filters by tag or category (see RF06). This is consistent with section 2: dynamic categorization was simplified to manual tags that receive no functional implementation.

6	/// The epic's ONE new DI-singleton access point for device-level access
7	/// (AD-14) — `core/navigation/app_router.dart`'s `_redirect` reads
8	/// [currentStatus] before it reads `SessionRepository.currentStatus`
9	/// (Boundaries: "`_redirect` checks `VaultStatus` before `SessionStatus`").
10	/// Mirrors `features/auth/domain/repositories/session_repository.dart`'s
11	/// shape, except [currentStatus] is never nullable (see [VaultStatus]'s own
12	/// doc) and there is no `restoreSession`-equivalent boot call — the vault
13	/// is always [VaultStatus.locked] until a successful [authenticate] call.
14	abstract class VaultRepository {
15	  /// Broadcast stream of the current vault status. Unlike
16	  /// `SessionRepository.statusStream`, this always has a value from the
17	  /// moment the repository is constructed ([VaultStatus.locked]) — a late
18	  /// subscriber still immediately replays that cached value, same
19	  /// `Stream.multi` rationale as the session repository's own stream.
20	  Stream<VaultStatus> get statusStream;
21	
22	  /// The last status emitted on [statusStream], read synchronously —
23	  /// starts at [VaultStatus.locked] (never `null`, see [VaultStatus]'s own
24	  /// doc) and only a successful [authenticate] call ever flips it to
25	  /// [VaultStatus.unlocked].
26	  VaultStatus get currentStatus;
27	
28	  /// Triggers the OS biometric prompt (`local_auth`, `biometricOnly: true`
29	  /// — Boundaries: "never set `biometricOnly: false`"). Zero network calls
30	  /// (Boundaries: "Vault makes zero network calls"); never produces
31	  /// [Failure.authInvalid] (reserved for password login) — any failure here
32	  /// (OS declines, cancels, or throws `LocalAuthException`) maps to
33	  /// [Failure.malformedResponse] instead, and [currentStatus] stays
34	  /// [VaultStatus.locked]. Only a `true` result flips [currentStatus] to
35	  /// [VaultStatus.unlocked] and emits it on [statusStream].
36	  Future<Either<Failure, Unit>> authenticate();
37	
38	  /// Story 2.2's biometric-failure fallback. No PIN-creation screen exists
39	  /// anywhere in `docs/input/` (Design Notes): the first call ever made to
40	  /// this method — regardless of which screen reached the keypad — stores
41	  /// [pin] as the vault's PIN and immediately succeeds; every later call
42	  /// compares [pin] against that stored value. A match (first-use or
43	  /// later) flips [currentStatus] to [VaultStatus.unlocked] and emits it on
44	  /// [statusStream], same as a successful [authenticate]. A mismatch never
45	  /// throws, never caps retries, and leaves [currentStatus] at
46	  /// [VaultStatus.locked] — [Failure.malformedResponse] is returned instead
47	  /// (RNF09), so the caller always has a retryable path, never a dead end.
48	  Future<Either<Failure, Unit>> submitPin(String pin);
49	
50	  /// Releases the underlying stream resource. Wired as `get_it`'s
51	  /// `dispose:` callback on registration, so `resetCoreDependencies()`
52	  /// (`sl.reset()`) closes it instead of leaking a `StreamController` on
53	  /// every test teardown.
54	  Future<void> dispose();
55	}

Report concisely (under 400 words) with file:line references for each finding, and your best read on whether there is an already-existing, safe way to make this link functionally navigate to /auth, or whether this would require adding new repository functionality that doesn't exist yet.

Story 2.2 (Biometric-Failure Fallback to PIN) is the explicit, already-planned owner of this distinction; revisit there rather than widening 2.1's error mapping speculatively now.
  resolved_by: Story 2.2 (code review, 2026-11-03) — every `authenticate()` failure now falls through to the same `PinKeypad`, so the lockout-vs-other-failure distinction this entry worried about is moot: there's no second OS-retry affordance to mis-route to regardless of which `LocalAuthExceptionCode` fired. `vault_repository_impl_test.dart` and `vault_lock_screen_test.dart` now each include a case exercising a `biometricLockout`-flavored failure to prove this explicitly rather than only by comment.

- source_spec: `_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/spec-2-1-biometric-pin-app-access-gate.md`
  summary: No timeout wraps the OS biometric prompt in `VaultLockScreen._attemptAuthenticate`; if `authenticate()` never resolves (a hung native call, not covered by `persistAcrossBackgrounding: true`), the lock screen stays on its initial "autenticando" state forever with no retry button and no escape — the one gate blocking every screen in the app.
  evidence: Outside spec-2-1's own I/O & Edge-Case Matrix, which only covers success/declined-or-cancelled, not a hang. No device/simulator exists yet (AGENTS.md) to reproduce or verify a real-world hang either way; revisit if this proves reachable in practice or once device testing exists.

- source_spec: `_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/spec-2-1-biometric-pin-app-access-gate.md`
  summary: `main.dart`'s `_CerneAppState.initState` fires `_sessionRepository.restoreSession()` (a real backend network call) unconditionally, with no gating on `VaultRepository.currentStatus` — in tension with `epic-2-context.md`'s own framing that "the vault gates whether anything may be shown at all, before any network/session state is considered."
  evidence: Unchanged since Story 1.4 (pre-existing, not introduced by this diff) — `VaultRepository` makes zero network calls itself (spec-2-1's own boundary), and this call's outcome only ever reaches the UI through `SessionStatus`/`statusStream`, which the vault gate already overrides while locked. A real architectural tension worth a deliberate decision once a later epic cares about exactly when the first network call fires relative to the vault, not a correctness bug in 2.1 itself.

  summary: Tapping "Usar PIN" switches `VaultLockScreen` to the PIN keypad but never cancels or acknowledges the still-pending native `authenticate()` call it escaped from — on a real device, the OS Face ID/Touch ID sheet may still be visible (or about to appear) underneath the app's own PIN keypad.
  evidence: `local_auth` exposes no universal cancel API for an in-flight `authenticate()` call, so there is no code-level fix available today — only a known-limitation to track. `_attemptAuthenticate`'s own `alreadyOnKeypad` guard already prevents the pending call's eventual result from clobbering the keypad's UI state once it resolves, but that doesn't address the native OS UI itself. ## Deferred from: code review of story-2-3-fixed-5-minute-idle-re-authentication-timeout (2026-11-03)

- source_spec: `_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/spec-2-3-fixed-5-minute-idle-re-authentication-timeout.md`
  summary: `VaultRepositoryImpl.didChangeAppLifecycleState`'s idle-timeout check computes elapsed time from wall-clock `DateTime.now()` (via the injectable `_now`), so a device clock change (manual adjustment, timezone shift, NTP correction) between `paused` and `resumed` can defeat or spuriously trigger the re-lock.
  evidence: This was a frozen, explicit boundary of spec-2-3 itself ("Elapsed time read via an injectable `DateTime Function() now` constructor param (default `DateTime.now`) for deterministic tests") rather than an implementation deviation. Kept for simplicity (no `clock`/`fake_async` dependency, matches Design Notes) rather than for any robustness reason — a monotonic source (e.g. `Stopwatch`) would avoid clock-tampering/skew, but isn't actually a stronger guarantee here: both approaches are lost identically if the app process is killed while backgrounded, since `VaultRepositoryImpl` itself is recreated on relaunch either way. Changing the device clock already requires the OS itself to be unlocked, so this only matters for Cerne's own vault layer specifically, not overall device access. Revisit if a stronger timing guarantee is ever required (e.g. hardening the vault beyond a reflective-journal app's current threat model).
